Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3811; uninstructed, i.e. (figuratively) stupid:--unlearned.
BiblicalUsage: Paul warns Timothy to avoid foolish and unlearned questions, knowing they do gender strifes. The word names the question no one has taught the asker to ask, the argument that has nothing to teach.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for unlearned questions carries no teaching of its own; its wisdom is Paul's, that some arguments are only good for breeding strife.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
